maps.name: Pendola Pass
maps.overview: Snowbound mountain pass added in the Frozen Trail 2.0 update (8 Oct 2026). The in-game map names nine areas, from the downed Fallen Emperor and Old Town in the west to the Railyard, Loading Platforms, Cielo Sereno Observatory and Deep-Space Telescope in the east.

notices.title: Gondola Transceivers are request points, not landing spots
notices.body: Use a Gondola Transceiver to call the gondola. The gondola may land some distance away from the transceiver. Plan your route to it, especially if you are downed or carrying a downed teammate. Landing locations are not marked on this map.

details.text: Early-access reports put the landing spot roughly 100–150 m from the transceiver you used, not at it.
Look for three cues once it is on its way: an incoming-gondola marker on your map, the transceiver light pointing toward the landing area, and green smoke rising where it will touch down.
The gondola carries three enclosed pods, one Raider per pod.

Players report a short countdown, about 10 seconds, that starts as soon as someone climbs in, even if the rest of the squad has not arrived. Treat this as a community observation; Embark has not published exact timings.
Calling the gondola is reported to attract ARC. Clear the area or call it from cover.

conditions.name: Redirection
conditions.description: Emperor Beacons are activating throughout the area. Raiders can loot and deploy them to redirect valuable payloads to their own position.

effects.name: Emperor Relays active
effects.note: Relay locations are event-specific and are not marked on the permanent map.

effects.name: Falling Debris
effects.note: Listed as an active hazard during Redirection.

effects.name: No Flash Freeze
effects.note: Listed by the game for this condition.

conditions.source: In-game destination screen (8 Oct 2026); Redirection is confirmed as a map condition in the official Frozen Trail 2.0 notes.
conditions.caveat: The steps and loot below come from early-access community reports and may change. No drop rates are published, and none are given here.

guide.title: Find a Damaged Emperor Relay
guide.text: Several relays appear across the map during Redirection. Players report a red beam and a relay icon marking each one.

guide.title: Search it for an Emperor Beacon
guide.text: Searching a relay is reported to give an Emperor Beacon. Players report carrying up to three.

guide.title: Deploy the beacon under open sky
guide.text: Place it somewhere with a clear view of the sky. The beacon beam is reported to be visible map-wide, so expect other squads to come looking.

guide.title: Take cover from the falling payload
guide.text: The payload comes down with debris that can hurt health and shields. Stay clear until it lands.

guide.title: Breach the payload, then sweep the debris
guide.text: The payload is reported to hold ARC Couplers (Conductive, Insulated and Plated) plus other ARC parts. Smaller debris reportedly drops ARC materials such as ARC Alloy, ARC Circuitry and ARC Motion Cores. Contents vary per payload.

guide.title: Craft the Emperor Gateway Conduit
guide.text: Community guides report the conduit is crafted at Workbench I from one of each coupler plus the Emperor Gateway Conduit Blueprint.

guide.title: Enter the Fallen Emperor
guide.text: The conduit is reported to open the way into the Fallen Emperor. Embark confirms only that an Emperor has fallen, that rare technology lies inside, and that Raiders must find a way in.

lootIntel.note: Loot types describe what a location tends to hold. High-value spawns can change from raid to raid, so no specific item is guaranteed anywhere.

locations.name: Fallen Emperor

caches.title: Frozen Raider Caches
caches.body: Pendola Pass has its own snow-covered version of the Raider Cache, opened with Breach & Search. Community data lists 13 cache clusters, each with several possible spots, and one spot used per raid. Exact spots are not shown here.
